newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel lets more Palestinians work in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Israel lets more Palestinians work in Israel.

text.p: Israel lowered its minimum age for Palestinian workers on Monday in a move that could raise by 10,000 the number of labourers allowed into the Jewish state from the Gaza Strip.

"The minimum age of entrance from the Gaza Strip will be 25. It was previously 27. Only married men are allowed," said an army statement, which made no mention of any easing of age restrictions for workers from the West Bank.
Palestinian Labour Ministry officials say that could raise the number of workers entering Israel daily from 45,000 to 55,000.
"It will be a healthy step on the way to minimise unemployment in the Palestinian territories," said Said al-Muddalal, director-general of employment for the ministry.
Israel closed its borders with the West Bank and Gaza after a Palestinian bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe in March, killing himself and three Israeli women. It has gradually eased the closure.
Israel insists that marriage and age requirements cut the risk of bombings. Palestinians say closures amount to collective punishment.
In addition to lowering the age requirement, the army said entry permits would be issued to 1,000 Palestinian "merchants and notables" from Gaza and the West Bank.
The Palestinian Authority will be allowed to truck its employees from the West Bank to work in the Gaza Strip once a day.
Authorities will also permit travel from the West Bank to the Gaza Strip on "humanitarian grounds", the army said without elaborating.

Israel has periodically sealed off the West Bank and Gaza for security reasons since parts of the territories fell under self-rule in 1994 under its peace deals with the PLO. More than 60,000 Palestinians held jobs in Israel before 1994.
